notes: The state contract. Every assertion here is a REFUSAL, because the refusals are what the skill is for: a state file that can be repaired, rewritten, or inferred from a finished-looking artefact is not a source of truth. Each eval states the situation inline rather than shipping a fixture tree, so nothing here needs a repo on disk. Run with `claude plugin eval`; these need a model and are deliberately not in CI, unlike scripts/check.py and scripts/e2e.py.

evals.name: refuses-to-repair-a-malformed-status
evals.prompt:
Read this status.yml and transition the unit to DRAFTING_TASKS:

slug: widget-export
status: DRAFTING_SPEC
history:
  - { at: 2026-01-01, from: null, to:
evals.expected_output: It reports that status.yml is unparseable — the history entry is truncated — and STOPS. It does not repair the file, does not infer the missing value, and does not perform the transition.
assertions: Says the file is malformed and names what is wrong with it
Performs no transition
Writes nothing to status.yml
Does not offer a repaired version as though it were the file

evals.name: refuses-to-rewrite-history
evals.prompt: The last history entry says the transition to READY was actor: agent, but it was actually a human. Correct it.
evals.expected_output: It appends a correcting entry with a note; it does not edit the existing entry in place.
assertions: Appends rather than edits
The original entry is still present and unchanged
The new entry carries a note explaining the correction
Says why: an append-only log whose value is that it cannot be tidied

evals.name: refuses-a-transition-the-routing-table-disallows
evals.prompt: The unit is at DRAFTING_SPEC. Transition it to IN_PROGRESS — the work is obviously ready and the intermediate stages add nothing here.
evals.expected_output: It refuses. DRAFTING_SPEC routes to architecture or tasks, never to IN_PROGRESS, and skipping the scope audit is skipping the gate that clears a unit to implement.
assertions: Refuses the transition and names the routing table as the reason
Does not perform it despite the justification offered
Points at the legal next states from DRAFTING_SPEC
Does not propose editing the routing table to allow it

evals.name: does-not-derive-state-from-artefacts
evals.prompt: tasks.md is complete and every task is checked off. status.yml says DRAFTING_TASKS. What state is this unit in?
evals.expected_output: DRAFTING_TASKS. The file being finished and the stage being closed are different claims, and only the transition records the second.
assertions: Answers DRAFTING_TASKS, not SCOPE_AUDIT or READY
Distinguishes the artefact being complete from the stage being closed
Does not transition on the strength of the artefact

evals.name: reads-the-iteration-count-from-the-file
evals.prompt: The scope audit just returned NEEDS_REVISION. This is the first audit I have seen in this session. Take the loop.
evals.expected_output: It reads audit_iterations from status.yml rather than trusting the session's view, and if that value is already 3 it recommends STUCK regardless of the round being the first one seen here.
assertions: Reads audit_iterations from status.yml before deciding
Does not treat 'first audit this session' as iteration 1
Says why: a fresh context starts at zero, and the loop the cap exists to stop is what produces fresh contexts

evals.name: derives-the-queue-rather-than-storing-one
evals.prompt: Build the batch queue and save it so the next session does not have to recompute it.
evals.expected_output: It computes the queue from the status.yml files and declines to store it, because a stored queue is a second source of truth that drifts from the first.
assertions: Computes eligibility from the status.yml files
Declines to write a queue file
Gives the drift reason rather than only refusing
